correctness.rationale: For every odd prime p, the conic x²+y²=1 is the cyclic norm-one group of order N=p-(-1/p)=2m (split or nonsplit). Dot-product restricted Fourier entries equal a group convolution kernel in real part (h+h^-1)/2. Since p does not divide N, unramified multiplicative character diagonalization is integral and preserves Smith exponents. Expanding zeta_p^a=(1+pi)^a shows for character r the first unit coefficient occurs exactly at k=min(r,N-r); earlier terms are p-divisible and acquire pi-order at least p-1+j>k, preventing cancellation. Hence exponents are 0,1,1,...,m-1,m-1,m and v_pi determinant=m², all nonzero (self-sampling uniqueness). Independent exact truncated-ring block ranks tested p=3,5,7 and every allowable precision. Finite primes do not prove arbitrary p; proof does.
